title: Lorentz force magnitude bound
references: Jackson, J. D., Classical Electrodynamics, 3rd ed., Wiley (1999)
Griffiths, D. J., Introduction to Electrodynamics, 4th ed., Cambridge University Press (2017)
validity_domain: Magnitude of the force on a point charge moving at speed `speed` in a field with electric magnitude `e_field` and magnetic magnitude `b_field`, all in one inertial frame. Bound: |F| = |q (E + v x B)| <= |q| (|E| + |v| |B|), by the triangle inequality and |v x B| <= |v| |B|.
limitations: Upper bound on the magnitude only: the equality needs E and v x B parallel, which the magnitudes alone do not tell, so a force below the bound is not confirmed
The fields and the speed are magnitudes given by the user; the directions are not modelled, so no vector quantity is used
Point charge, fields at the position of the charge, no radiation reaction, no field produced by the charge itself
Valid in any inertial frame with the fields and the speed measured in that frame; the force is the rate of change of momentum there

variables.b_field: Magnitude of the magnetic flux density
